title: Answer: no position on free will, and biological agency serves goals of the system's own

statements.text: Predictive processing, in Seth's account, takes no position on whether there is free will. Volition enters as one dimension of the experienced self, the volitional self, made of experiences of intention and of agency, which like other parts of the self the brain generates. On agency, biological agency is more than acting in the service of goals: its goals are typically the system's own rather than imposed from outside, and rich embodiment may be needed for it.
statements.scope: the essay on the real problem (2016) and Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism (2025, accepted manuscript), section 5.7

sources.quote: The volitional self involves experiences of intention and of agency
the brain actively and continuously generates and coordinates these diverse aspects of self-experience.
In biological systems, the relevant goals are typically endogenous, rather than being exogenously imposed
Rich embodiment and embeddedness might be needed for a system to possess or exhibit agency in this sense
